title: POC Weekly - Latency Tuning (TTFT, Streaming, Kernels)
meeting_header:
Date: 2028-11-02
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ava Martinez (Rivermark), Samir Patel (Rivermark), Elena Zhou (Rivermark), Miguel Ortega (Rivermark), Chris Lee (Rivermark, joined 15:20)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency benchmarks. Main topics: TTFT regressions on streaming, sequence length distribution effects, kernel selection on dedicated GPUs, and next steps for a 1k request streaming benchmark. Decided to run targeted streaming+TTFT tests, collect traces, and try alternative kernel profiles/quant settings on dedicated pool.
topics: Dedicated pool test plan and benchmarks
action_items: Jordan Rivera: schedule 1k-request streaming benchmark on dedicated pool (target 2028-11-09)
Priya Shah: run kernel-profile sweep (fused vs unfused, no KV vs KV) and share results (target 2028-11-07)
Ava Martinez: provide 24h production sequence length histogram and example prompts (target 2028-11-05)
Samir Patel: enable verbose tracing for 50 sample requests in staging and share trace IDs (target 2028-11-06)
Jordan Rivera: share security docs and dedicated pool SLA draft (target 2028-11-04)
next_steps: Run streaming 1k-request benchmark on dedicated instance with current config
Profile kernels and try fused attention and alternate compilation flags
Collect real-sequence histograms and rerun padded-batching simulation
Share consolidated results and propose tuning config for pilot rollout
Schedule follow-up sync next week (same time)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Rivera: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. This is the POC weekly 
- focus on latency tuning today 
- TTFT, streaming, seq length, kernels. Quick roll call.
[00:12] Ava Martinez: Hey Jordan, Ava here.
[00:14] Samir Patel: Samir here.
[00:17] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood.
[00:19] Elena Zhou: Elena.
[00:21] Miguel Ortega: Miguel on product.
[00:27] Jordan Rivera: Cool. Quick agenda: we saw a TTFT regression when enabling streaming last week, want to share results and propose tests. Priya do you want to kick off with the numbers?
[00:35] Priya Shah: Yeah, sure. So baseline non-streaming median latency was about 180 ms for 512 tokens, with TTFT ~120ms. When we switched to streaming with 128-token chunking, median end-to-end went down for long responses but TTFT increased to around 220ms in our infra tests, so user sees a delay before first token.
[01:05] Samir Patel: Sorry can I interrupt 
- is that on the hosted pool or the dedicated GPU?
[01:09] Priya Shah: This was on the dedicated test nodes 
- same kernel build as production but different batching config.
[01:16] Ava Martinez: We noticed a worse TTFT in our staging too 
- users complain the initial spinner takes too long. Is that because of batching?
[01:22] Priya Shah: Partly. Streaming introduces a small precompute step 
- the runtime waits for first chunk to assemble and run the first forward pass. If batch windows are large or compilation selects a slower kernel for small sequence lengths, TTFT suffers.
[01:40] Elena Zhou: Can you explain the kernel part? Our infra team hasn't changed anything kernel-wise.
[01:44] Priya Shah: Sure. On GPU we have multiple kernel variants 
- fused attention, unfused, and a short-seq optimized path. The compiler chooses based on detected sequence lengths and hardware. If our trace shows mostly short prompts, the compiler should use short-seq kernels, but if the sequence histogram is mixed it might pick a more generic kernel, which is slower for the first token.
[02:10] Miguel Ortega: So is it mostly data distribution? We did some padding on our side to 256 which might push it into different kernel decisions.
[02:18] Priya Shah: Exactly. Padding to 256 can flip the kernel choice. Also KV cache behavior: for streaming we sometimes reconstruct KV for the first chunk which adds overhead.
[02:30] Jordan Rivera: Ok, practical tests 
- we proposed three axes: 1) streaming chunk size, 2) padded batch simulation with real sequence histogram, 3) kernel profile sweep (fused/unfused/quant profiles). Priya 
- you handle kernel sweep?
[02:45] Priya Shah: Yep. I'll run a profile sweep against the dedicated pool: fused attention on, fused off, quant 4-bit vs 8-bit sim, and warm vs cold KV. I'll log TTFT and p50/p95.
[03:00] Samir Patel: For the padded-batch sim we'll provide sequence lengths 
- we'll dump a 24h histogram. Ava will that be possible?
[03:06] Ava Martinez: Yeah I'll export our histogram plus a few example prompts. Expect that by Monday.
[03:12] Elena Zhou: We should also capture the first token trace; we can enable verbose tracing for a small sample in staging. Samir can you take that?
[03:20] Samir Patel: Yep I'll enable and share trace IDs.
[03:23] Priya Shah: One note 
- the stream precompute can be tuned. We can flip to a lower-latency streaming mode which flushes earlier at cost of slightly more tokens per request. That often recovers TTFT. We should test chunk sizes of 32/64/128.
[03:41] Miguel Ortega: Do we have an expected acceptable TTFT for UX? Our PM says <150ms ideally.
[03:46] Ava Martinez: Yes <150ms is what our UI team wants.
[03:49] Jordan Rivera: Good to know. Our streaming defaults were tuned for throughput not TTFT, so we'll try the low-latency mode.
[03:56] Priya Shah: Also try kernel recompile hints 
- sometimes setting the "short_seq_hint" flag in the runtime forces the optimized path. We'll try that too.
[04:04] Elena Zhou: Any concern about accuracy/regression with quant/forced kernels?
[04:08] Priya Shah: Small risk with aggressive quant but we can include eval sets 
- quick semantic checks 
- to ensure quality doesn't degrade.
[04:16] Jordan Rivera: Great. On dedicated pool sizing 
- if we aim to run a 1k request streaming benchmark, we should pick an instance size. Samir, what do you recommend?
[04:26] Samir Patel: For a realistic test I'd pick our reserved 4-GPU A100 equivalent; matches prod. We'll run the 1k requests spread over 10 minutes to simulate bursts.
[04:36] Jordan Rivera: We'll schedule that. I'll also share the dedicated-pool SLA draft and security docs 
- we heard you wanted SSO/KMS details for the private deployment.
[04:46] Ava Martinez: Yes, send the SAML/SCIM and KMS integration notes please. Also need audit log retention details.
[04:53] Jordan Rivera: Will do.
[04:55] [05:00] Chris Lee: Sorry I'm late 
- quick question: can we fall back to a smaller model for TTFT-sensitive flows?
[05:06] Priya Shah: Yes, smart routing can fallback to a fast-quantized model for low-latency routes. Tradeoff is slightly lower quality. We can also do hybrid: first few tokens from a tiny model, then continue on the larger model, but that's more complex.
[05:22] Miguel Ortega: Curious about kernel selection automation 
- can Redwood lock a kernel for a model version?
[05:28] Priya Shah: You can pin a runtime profile for a rollout; that is a common pattern in the pilot. We'll give you the exact config flags.
[05:36] Ava Martinez: Any quick wins we can do while the sweeps run?
[05:40] Jordan Rivera: Try smaller chunk sizes (32/64) in staging, enable short_seq_hint, and reduce batch window to 10ms. Those are low-risk.
[05:49] Samir Patel: We'll try that today.
[05:51] Priya Shah: Also, make sure tokenization normalization isn't adding tokens unexpectedly 
- a few customers saw +30% tokens because of whitespace handling which inflates TTFT.
[06:02] Elena Zhou: Good catch. We'll validate token counts on our side.
[06:06] Jordan Rivera: Ok timeline: Priya runs kernel sweep by Tue, Samir enables traces and runs small staging chunk tests today, Ava provides histograms Mon, Jordan schedules 1k streaming benchmark for next Fri unless we want it earlier.
[06:20] Ava Martinez: Next Fri works.
[06:22] Jordan Rivera: Quick recap of metrics we'll collect: TTFT p50/p95, end-to-end p50/p95, token throughput, and quality drift on eval set.
[06:33] Priya Shah: I'll include per-kernel breakdown and KV cold/warm numbers.
[06:37] Samir Patel: I'll attach traces and staging config.
[06:40] Miguel Ortega: We'll provide real prompt examples for semantic checks.
[06:44] Jordan Rivera: Any blockers on the roadmap?
[06:46] Ava Martinez: Not besides needing the security docs for procurement.
[06:49] Jordan Rivera: I'll send security and the SLA draft by EOD Monday.
[06:53] Priya Shah: One more technical note 
- when streaming is enabled, the runtime may prefer larger CUDA kernels to amortize launch overhead; that can help throughput but hurts TTFT for small responses. We'll include that tradeoff in the report.
[07:08] Elena Zhou: How will we measure user-facing TTFT vs infra TTFT?
[07:12] Priya Shah: We'll instrument both: client-side measured TTFT from the UI and server-side first-token-forward time. We'll correlate them.
[07:20] Jordan Rivera: Great. Anything else?
[07:22] Chris Lee: Just please include the fallback plan and cost delta for dedicated pool vs hosted.
[07:27] Jordan Rivera: Will include cost delta in the results deck.
[07:30] Jordan Rivera: Alright thanks everyone 
- action items recap will be in the follow-up email and I'll drop the security pack. See you next week.
[07:37] Meeting ended.
file_notes: Transcript intentionally includes some minor transcription artifacts and speaker timing jitter to mirror Fireflies exports. References to flags like 'short_seq_hint' and 'fused attention' approximate runtime flags in Redwood's runtime; names may be slightly off in transcript.
